title: Mutation-id correlation layer; ErrorData/map dual-shape decode copied 7 times
note: Verified: the typed-vs-map switch exists at app_rpc.go:677 and 903 (stamp), app_restart_required.go:301 (read) and 318 (stamp three fields), web_api.go:62 and 82 (read), appsource/source.go:612 (read), plus the re-marshal variant at app_retirement_resume.go:22 and clientMutationIDFromData. 8 'clientMutationId is required' checks confirmed (app_rpc.go:1664..1934). app_rpc.go has 102 commits / 29 'fix' since Sep 1. Overstated: it is ~430 lines (487-917), and the sites are two operations (read a field, stamp fields), not 7 identical copies; the stamp variants stamp different field sets, and the policy prose is mostly legitimate rules. Drift risk is real but modest, so high is too strong.
revised_fix_plan: Add appwire helpers: ErrorDataOf(WireError) (typed/map/embedded) for the read sites and a WithErrorData(wire, func(*ErrorData) / map setter) for the stamp sites; migrate the 7 sites. Add a requireClientMutationID helper for the 8 checks. Do NOT bother moving the 14 correlation functions into a new file unless a PR touches them anyway. Table test over typed/map/embedded shapes first.

title: registerThreadHandlers repeats one handler skeleton and re-implements resume-retry for turn/start
note: Skeleton repetition confirmed (8 id checks, same withDeletionTargetOwnership + adoptCallerMutationResult shape). But turn/start is NOT a duplicate of withSessionResume: its first attempt resolves the source inside the retried closure and resumes even when resolution failed (app_rpc.go:1763-1770), it has a distinct resumeAfterConfirmedRetirement branch (1773-1790) and a different initial-failure filter. Folding it into withSessionResume, or 'deleting the quirk', changes behavior on the hottest path.
revised_fix_plan: Add requireClientMutationID plus a small helper owning the trailing adoptCallerMutationResult for the 7 non-start mutation handlers. For turn/start, only share the retry tail (retryAfterResume correlation) with withSessionResume after hub-app-rest-5 removes the dead firstAttemptPreDispatch branch; keep the resolve-failure-resumes and retiring-daemon paths as they are. Behavior-pinning table test for missing id -> InvalidParams across the 8 handlers (assert code, not copy).

title: Endpoint-fingerprint guard ~900 lines with near-identical verifiers and fail-closed default
note: Verified: verifyEndpointFingerprintWithKey (app_auth.go:1404), verifyFlowEndpointWithKey (1486) and verifyConfigRevision share the empty-assertion / empty-current / mismatch shape; LoginStart (app_auth.go:402-405) and DeviceStart (1092-1095) carry the identical start-time guard; platform key files total 245 lines (31+94+120). resolveEndpointFingerprintKey has 22 non-test and 45 total references (not 19). Corrections: docs/product/subsystems.md S15 already states a guarantee ('an endpoint change refuses the pending completion', the in-flight probe fence), so 'docs/product has no entry' is wrong for flows; only the key-file mechanism and fail-closed-on-unkeyable behavior are undocumented. Churn is low (one endpoint-related commit since Sep 1), so severity high is not supported. Phase 2 (replace mechanism) touches a credential-safety boundary and must be Jesse's call.
revised_fix_plan: Phase 1 only: one endpointGuard.Check(asserted, current, keyErr, messages) shared by the three verifiers, hoist the duplicated start-time check into one helper, drop the unkeyed wrappers that only tests call (hub-app-rest-7). Phase 2: ask Jesse whether the HMAC key-file mechanism and its fail-closed refusal on unkeyable state match the recovery-over-lockdown stance; document the decision in S15 before any removal.

title: Four 'load or create 0600 secret' implementations
note: Four load-or-create-under-state-dir functions exist, but they implement different policies: the hub key rotates a wrong-mode/foreign-owner/empty file under a cross-process lock (app_instances.go:611-778); llm/continuation_secret.go:readContinuationSecret FAILS on a non-0600 mode (opposite policy); hubedge writes a trimmed base64 token via temp+rename with no mode check; installid is an afero-based installation id with its own advisory lock, not a secret. A common helper needs a policy option for exactly the behavior that differs, and the -300 LOC estimate is optimistic. Consolidating would also change which failure each caller surfaces.
revised_fix_plan: Skip the four-way consolidation. If anything, share only the publish primitive (O_EXCL temp 0600 + fsync + link/rename) between the hub key and hubedge, leaving each caller's validation policy in place. Revisit only if a fifth copy appears.

title: Giant lifecycle functions with repeated alias-group fencing
note: Sizes confirmed: forceStopThread is app_force_stop.go:53-450 (398 lines), hubThreadFork 1076-1304 (229). Refuted part: the 'validate every alias deletion fence then take reservations' pattern is not four copies of one thing. The fence check is already one shared helper (deletionFenceErrorForGroup, used at app_force_stop.go:120,258,374,571,598,673, app_daemons.go:344, app_retirement_resume.go:217, app_threadlifecycle.go:552,659); only force-stop takes tryLockForceStopReservations; fork uses sorted lockDeletionTarget and deletionFenceErrorNaming; retire/resume do not reserve. A lockAliasGroup helper would unify things that deliberately differ in ordering.
revised_fix_plan: Split forceStopThread (and, separately, hubThreadFork) into named phase functions guarded by the existing force-stop and fork tests. Drop the lockAliasGroup extraction.

title: Fork capability fences defined twice with a manual parity contract
note: Parity comments confirmed (app_threadread.go:755 and :801 'a fence added here is owed there too'). But the two sides already share the core predicates (hubForkLiveDelegateFenced, hubForkIdentityFenced, hubForkRecoveryFenced are used by both capability and RPC; the comments say so). What remains duplicated is which predicates are called per identity. The RPC also does lock-time epoch sampling, ownership recheck and deletion-before-recovery ordering (app_threadlifecycle.go:1100-1215) that a lock-free capability projection cannot reuse, so a single forkAdmission returning a refusal is not a drop-in and -150 LOC is unrealistic.
revised_fix_plan: Add only a parity table test: for each fence input (live delegate, recovery flag, roster recovery, resolved-session fence, deletion fence), assert the capability projection is false exactly when the RPC refuses. No new abstraction.
